title: Self-healing search index: auto-rebuild on staleness or corruption
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: .boreal/runtime/search-index.json is a rebuildable derived artifact, yet when it is stale or corrupt the agent gets an error and improvises (6 vault init calls in the audit). Change: when a command detects the search.index-stale gap (already in enforcement-gaps.ts) or index corruption, rebuild the index once automatically under a lock, then proceed; only surface an error if the rebuild itself fails, and that error must carry the task-3 terminal payload pointing at doctor. Where: index load path in packages/engine/src/runtime.ts, existing search index command in apps/cli/src/commands.ts, lock via the existing lock machinery (lock inspect/break exist). Constraint: exactly one rebuild per detection even under concurrent commands (lock-guarded); rebuild must be from ledgers, the durable source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: A stale or corrupt search index triggers exactly one automatic lock-guarded rebuild and the original command then succeeds
Two concurrent commands hitting a stale index produce one rebuild, not two (test)
Rebuild failure surfaces a terminal error pointing at doctor, never a retry loop
